title: Decompose monolithic merge worker; introduce aggregation shards to reduce tail latency
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: The current console aggregation pipeline relies on a single merge worker that serializes many GraphQL resolver results and performs synchronous fan‑in merging. Under bursty read patterns this worker experiences head-of-line locking and causes 99.9th percentile tail latency spikes for dashboard and rollout pages. We also see elevated memory churn from large in‑flight response objects and repeated rehydration of the same prefix cache across requests.

Goal: Reduce tail latency and memory pressure by decomposing the merge worker into multiple lighter-weight aggregation shards, add non-blocking streaming merge paths for low‑latency queries, and introduce an async read‑through snapshot cache for hot prefixes. Secondary goals: simplify backpressure signals from the HTTP layer to workers and enable per‑shard CPU/memory autoscaling in Dedicated deployments.

Scope: This ticket covers the server-side changes in the console backend aggregator service and related GraphQL resolver wiring. It includes: 1) creating per‑tenant or per‑cohort aggregation shards, 2) moving large response serialization off the hot path into background processor, 3) adding streaming merge fastpath for <200ms targets, and 4) a small schema bump for the aggregator RPC to support partial result streaming. UI changes are out of scope (console will consume same API surface).
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end 99.9th percentile latency for console dashboard API reduced by >=45% on the benchmark suite (see benchmarks link)
Peak memory per aggregator process reduced by >=30% under synthetic 10x burst load
No functional regressions: existing GraphQL fields and rollouts render identically when compared against golden snapshots
Aggregator can be scaled by shard independently and exposes shard-level metrics in the console (requests/sec, max-latency, queue-depth)
Streaming merge path returns partial responses below 200ms for 80% of small queries in the benchmark and falls back gracefully to full merge when not supported
implementation_notes: Design doc: implement shallow decomposition where each shard owns a subset of keys by hashing (cohort/customer/route) with a sticky assignment map stored in etcd; avoid global rebalancing in this iteration
RPC change: extend aggregation_v2.MergeRequest with optional 'streaming_hint' boolean and 'max_partial_size' integer; add MergePartial event to the RPC stream

Cache: introduce async snapshot cache backed by Redis for hot prefix snapshots. Reads first consult shard local in-memory small LRU then fall back to Redis snapshot; evictions via TTL + explicit invalidation from write path

Serialization: offload large JSON payload assembly to a background worker pool; frontdoor returns 202 + temp handle for very large responses (>1.5MB) until serialized, but default path keeps synchronous behavior for small responses
Backpressure: expose queue-depth and offer TTL-based early reject for requests that would exceed configured per-shard queue (configurable by tier)
Compatibility: keep existing aggregator endpoints while launching /aggregation_v2; graceful flag flip managed via runtime config and feature flagged per-deployment
Testing: add fault-injection harness for per-shard failures so we can validate fallback to global merge during partial outage

Rollout plan: 1) deploy aggregation_v2 in read-only mirrors, 2) enable streaming fastpath for internal canary orgs, 3) incremental ramp to 30%/60%/100% with health checks and auto-rollback on error rate increase
benchmarks: Baseline (console-2025.09 cluster): dashboard-api 99.9p = 1.2s, p95 = 220ms, mean memory per aggregator = 1.2GB
Target after shard rollout: 99.9p <= 650ms (>=45% reduction), p95 <= 120ms, mean memory per aggregator <= 800MB
Streaming fastpath target for small queries: 80% of responses <200ms end-to-end in staging harness
